Not everyone knows this (and I won't pretend I did), but Apple has published incredibly detailed dimensional drawings for dozens of devices to help accessory manufacturers design compatible products. Here are the details.

Apple Hardware, Fully Exposed

For nearly thirty years, Jason Kottke has been one of my primary sources for finding interesting things on the internet (and beyond), and I'm sure there are countless things I would never have found without him.

A few days ago, he posted a link to the "Dimensional drawings" section of the accessories area of Apple's developer site.

In short, this is a database of highly detailed technical drawings, currently covering 96 devices, including the new iPhone 18 Pro, Apple Watch Ultra 4 and Series 12, and AirPods 5.

The list also includes products like MacBook Neo and Siri Remote, as well as accessories like AirTag, AirPods charging cases, and Apple Vision Pro ZEISS lens accessories.

Each document contains precise measurements, from overall device dimensions and curvatures to buttons, lenses, sensors, speakers, and ports, along with detailed "keepout zone" markings indicating where specific materials cannot be placed.

Although these documents are primarily intended for accessory manufacturers, anyone with even a passing interest in hardware, industrial design, or just that meticulous quality of Apple products should find them worth a look.

To view Apple's dimensional drawings, please click this link. If you don't yet follow kottke.org, you should start immediately.
